results.title: Lake Powell reaching critically low elevation levels, nearing 'dead ...
results.content:
Lake Powell, the second-largest reservoir in the U.S., is nearing critically low water elevation levels, the latest data shows.

As of Monday, water levels at Lake Powell measured at 3,524.3 feet above sea level, according to the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation tracker. [...] Water supplies in Lake Powell are currently dwindling dangerously close -- about 4 feet -- to the previous record set in April 2023 at 3,520 feet, driven by a decades-long megadrought. The rate of decline has leveled off in recent weeks, running around 2 feet higher than previous projections, which suggests that mitigation efforts could be helping somewhat. [...] Lake Powell currently has about 5.52 million acre-feet of large storage and has lost about 4,800 acre-feet of water per day since June 1, Schmidt said.

Reservoir operations can get "very complicated" once elevation drops below 3,500 feet and live storage drops below 4.3 million acre-feet, Schmidt said. At that point, the Bureau of Reclamation would "be seriously concerned," he added.

results.title: Lake Powell Water Level Update: Map of States Demanding $2B From Congress - Newsweek
results.content:
Early morning sunlight hits canyon walls on Lake Powell in the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area on July 10, 2025, in Page, Arizona.

## Lake Powell Water Level Update

As of Tuesday's data, Lake Powell's water level was at 3,526.4 feet elevation, roughly 31 feet lower than during this time last year and 35 feet lower than in 2024. The lake's levels have been plunging since last June and it is only 23 percent full. [...] According to basin officials, Lake Powell is approaching elevations that place hydropower generation at risk, prompting immediate drought response measures this year. If water levels fall too low, power production becomes less efficient or could cease altogether, forcing utilities to rely more heavily on alternative energy sources that may be more expensive or carbon-intensive. [...] As Congress weighs its response, Lake Powell continues to serve as a stark indicator of the West’s water future. The reservoir’s water level is no longer just a local concern; it is a shared national challenge with implications for food security, energy reliability, ecosystems and millions of lives across the Colorado River Basin.

Projections of end of water year 2026 elevation using the July minimum and May maximum inflow forecast results from the 24-Month Study model run are 3,516.18 feet and 3,517.25 feet, respectively. results.title: Water Levels | EROS
results.content:
Drought combined with water withdrawals has caused a drop in the lake’s water level. The reservoir finished filling in 1980. The highest water level recorded was in July 1983. The lowest was in April 2023, when the lake level was down about 185 feet from its high mark.

On the chart, the numbers on the left indicate feet above sea level for the lake’s water level. A water level of 3,700 feet is the reservoir at full capacity.
